\paragraph{Implications for robot learning.}
No $\dt$-embedding-dependent CIVO was observed in manipulation (Table~\ref{tab:cross_domain}). Both domains use dense shaped rewards, so reward sparsity cannot explain the boundary. A preliminary hypothesis is that locomotion's periodic state-action dynamics create stronger dependence on RSSM temporal prediction accuracy---small $\dt$-conditioned reward biases compound over cyclical gaits---whereas manipulation's contact-gated transitions are less sensitive to temporal conditioning fidelity. Other possible mediators include action-space periodicity and observation structure; the precise factors remain an open question.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Scope precision through negative controls.}
Six environments across three task types (Table~\ref{tab:cross_env_civo}, Table~\ref{tab:cross_domain}) delineate when CIVO does and does not occur: multi-joint locomotion reliably triggers it (5/7 seeds, two environments); single-joint dynamics (Cartpole, 0/3) and manipulation (three ManiSkill tasks, 0/3 trigger-specific) do not. Both locomotion and manipulation use dense shaped rewards, so reward sparsity cannot explain the boundary. A preliminary hypothesis is that locomotion's periodic state-action dynamics create stronger dependence on RSSM temporal prediction accuracy---small $\dt$-conditioned reward biases compound over cyclical gaits---whereas manipulation's contact-gated transitions are less sensitive to temporal conditioning fidelity. This precision is a feature of the experimental design: the negative controls confirm that the NVE diagnostic and frozen-embedding fix target the identified failure mode specifically, not benign value-ratio transients in non-locomotion domains.
